title: config_list
description: Result of bare `stride config` — every config key that holds a value, sorted by key, each MARKED rather than filtered. Names only, never values: a listing is a different question from a lookup, and returning values would be one command that dumps every secret, going around `config get`'s per-key redaction. `redacted: true` marks the entries `config get` will refuse to show, so a caller can tell 'set, and I may read it' from 'set, and I may not' without a call per key. Keys are NOT filtered out, because hiding a row the engine ignores makes it undiscoverable while leaving it in the database — see `status`.

status.description: `read` — the engine consults this key. `derived` — stored and ignored: the `ftp*` family, computed from power history (ADR 0005), which `config get` answers `derived_key` for; these are the rows most likely to be present on a real database, since it predates the derivation. `unrecognised` — a retired name, or a row written by a `config set` typo before #254 refused them. Only `read` keys have a payload `config get` will return, which is what `just schema-check` selects on.
